transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-12
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Menon (CTO - Starlake), Carlos Vega (Head of Cloud Eng), Anita Rao (Security)

Agenda:
- Run through Starlake success criteria for POC
- Network topology options: VPC peering vs PrivateLink/Private Endpoints
- Data residency and region constraints (EU requirement for subset of workload)
- Benchmarks: throughput/latency targets and test plan
- Timeline and next steps

Summary:
Quick scoping call. Starlake wants a Private deployment POC to validate private networking (no public egress), EU data residency for PHI-adjacent workloads, and benchmarks showing 95th percentile latency < 120ms for inference and sustained throughput ~200 requests/min with bursts. Redwood AE+SE explained Dedicated vs Private options, recommended Private (VPC peering + PrivateLink) for their compliance needs, and agreed to run a benchmark harness. Action items and next steps enumerated at the end. Transcription has some small mis-hears.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: okay thanks everyone for jumping on, um this is Maya from Redwood, i'll hand it over to Liam for the deep network bits after a quick run through goals
00:10 Dr. Priya Menon: yeah thanks, we wanted to make sure this POC covers private networking and EU data residency, like we can't have inference payloads egress to public internet for the EU customers, that is non-negotiable
00:25 Carlos Vega: hi all, from cloud side, we run primarily in eu-west-1 for the EMEA tenants, some us-west for domestic. our ask is - can Redwood's private deployment host in eu-west-1 and we can peer? or do you only do us regions?
00:40 Maya Chen: good question. we have Redwood Private options in multiple regions, eu-west-1 is supported. you can either do VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink depending on your network posture. Liam, quick take?
00:50 Liam Ortiz: yeah so we typically recommend PrivateLink for cross-account isolation and when customers don't want route table changes. VPC peering is simpler but you need to manage CIDR overlap and routing, and if you have Transit Gateway we can support that too. also note stuff around egress — if you require no public egress we can ensure all inference traffic stays on the private network path, but you'll want to mirror our recommended NAT/route config.
01:12 Anita Rao: can we get something written about encryption keys. KMS/HSM, and who controls keys, we have a policy that keys for eu data must be in eu KMS and customer-managed ideally
01:25 Maya Chen: absolutely, we support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments and HSM integrations for enterprise tiers. i'll attach the security whitepaper with the exact controls.
01:35 Dr. Priya Menon: perfect. on benchmarks - we need numbers. target is 95th percentile under 120ms for typical prompts, and throughput of about 200 req/min per model with peak bursts to 2k requests in a 10 minute window. can you simulate that?
01:50 Liam Ortiz: yes we can. for the POC we typically do a sim with 1) steady-state load 200 rpm, 2) burst test to 2k over 10m, and 3) long tail latency profile. we will need your sample prompts and average token lengths. also let us know model sizes (you want open LLM or a smaller quantized variant).
02:12 Carlos Vega: sample prompt sizes are around 40-80 tokens output, with some longer report-generation up to 250 tokens. we might prefer a 7B quantized model for cost but need perf numbers at both 7B and 13B.
02:28 Liam Ortiz: okay we'll include 7B and 13B variants. note that quantization changes KV cache behavior — sometimes you see latency delta; we'll test with continuous batching and prefix cache enabled.
02:42 Maya Chen: can i ask about egress costs — Starlake is sensitive to cross-region egress charges. if we deploy in eu-west-1 and you peer from your us hub, any egress would be billed via your cloud bill. generally with PrivateLink/VPC peering we can keep traffic intra-region to avoid inter-region egress, but if your control plane is in a different region please flag that.
03:05 Carlos Vega: our control plane is in eu-west-1 too, whether we use an on-prem transit device or TGW depends. we prefer Peer over PrivateLink if latency is critical, but security might push us to PrivateLink.
03:20 Anita Rao: also SOC2/ISO requirements — do you retain logs? we need audit logs turned on but restricted retention. does Redwood provide audit exports to our audit bucket?
03:34 Liam Ortiz: yes for Private we can stream audit logs to a customer S3 in their account, and configure retention. We'll also support token-level metrics but we can redact content if needed. note sometimes automatic exports include truncated metadata, we'll document that.
03:50 Maya Chen: quick note - when we talk about 'Private' here, it's the Redwood Private package (customer-managed VPC peer or PrivateLink) — unlike Dedicated which is reserved GPU pools managed by Redwood but possibly with shared network constraints. for strict egress/data residency go Private.
04:08 Dr. Priya Menon: timeline - we need the POC completed before end of Jan for exec review. is that realistic?
04:15 Liam Ortiz: yes if we start the week of Dec 21 with network setup and credentials, we can run benchmarks in the first two weeks of Jan and deliver results by Jan 22. that assumes we get the VPC CIDRs and peering contacts by Dec 14.
04:32 Carlos Vega: we can share VPC diagram by Dec 14. also would like a handshake test — simple ping/tcp test — before the full benchmark so we can validate routing and security groups.
04:45 Liam Ortiz: we'll do a smoke test, then ramp to steady-state, then bursts. we'll provide the test harness (k6 + custom generator) and a short runner script you can run from your env.
04:58 Anita Rao: on contractual side, we need a clause on data residency and a statement of where data is at rest. Also SSO integration — we use Okta, SAML 2.0.
05:10 Maya Chen: we support SSO via SAML and can map groups to RBAC. i'll include the SSO setup doc. for data residency we'll provide the deployment manifest that pins region and storage to eu-west-1.
05:22 Dr. Priya Menon: any blockers we should call out now?
05:27 Carlos Vega: ports - we need to know which ports Redwood requires for peering/PrivateLink and whether we need to open any egress to licensing endpoints — we try to avoid outbound internet from our VPC.
05:40 Liam Ortiz: good call. for PrivateLink there are no outbound egress to internet for runtime; control-plane calls for billing/telemetry can be routed through an allowed list if you prefer. we'll put exact CIDRs and ports in the checklist.
05:55 Maya Chen: cool. recap before we close — next steps: Maya sends network checklist + security whitepaper + SOC2 snapshots; Liam shares benchmark plan and test harness; Carlos shares VPC diagram by Dec 14; Anita shares compliance matrix; schedule smoke test week of Dec 21. any other items?
06:12 Dr. Priya Menon: no, that covers it, thanks. excited to see the latency numbers.
06:18 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the docs and calendar invites. bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription fidelity: occasional mis-hears around specific product keywords (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'KV cash' in one segment). Speaker labels are accurate for the most part but may show brief overlap.
